source_title: 101 Questions To Ask Yourself in Life
attribution: Adapted from 101 Questions To Ask Yourself in Life by Personal Excellence (https://personalexcellence.co/blog/101-questions/)

items.title: Who are you?
items.body: How would you describe yourself?

items.title: What are you passionate about?
What past achievements are you proudest of?
What are you grateful for?
What are the most important things to you in life?
What are your values?
items.body: (Values are principles that you regard as most important, that you wish to embody as a person.)

items.title: On a scale of 1-10, how much do you love yourself?
items.body: Why did you give this score?

items.title: Is it 10/10?
items.body: If not, how can you achieve a 10/10 self-love?
context: On a scale of 1-10, how much do you love yourself? Why did you give this score?

items.title: What is your ideal self?
items.body: What qualities does he/she have?

items.title: How can you be more like your ideal self?
context: What is your ideal self? What qualities does he/she have?

items.title: Look at your life now
items.body: On a scale of 1-10, how happy are you with your life? Why did you give this score?

items.title: How can you increase your happiness level?
context: Look at your life now. On a scale of 1-10, how happy are you with your life? Why did you give this score?

items.title: If you have a year left to live, what would you do?
If you only have a week left to live, what would you do?
If you only have a day left to live, what would you do?
If you only have a minute left to live, what would you do?
What are the biggest things you’ve learned in life to date?
What advice would you give to your younger self?
Imagine you are 10 years older
items.body: What advice would you give to your present self?

items.title: What are your Quadrant 2 tasks?
items.body: (Quadrant 2 tasks are the important but not urgent things on our to-do list.)

items.title: How can you start working on them?
context: What are your Quadrant 2 tasks? (Quadrant 2 tasks are the important but not urgent things on our to-do list.)

items.title: What are the things that normally keep you busy, but are unimportant?
Can you discard them?
items.body: If not, how can you streamline, automate, or delegate them?
context: What are the things that normally keep you busy, but are unimportant?

items.title: What are your biggest goals and dreams?
If you were to do something for free for the rest of your life, what would it be?
What would you do if you cannot fail — if there are no limitations in money, resources, time, or networks?
How can you make this happen, even if in a small way?
context: What would you do if you cannot fail — if there are no limitations in money, resources, time, or networks?

items.title: What do you want to achieve 1 year from now?
…3 years?
context: What do you want to achieve 1 year from now?

items.title: …5 years?
context: What do you want to achieve 1 year from now?
…3 years?

items.title: …10 years?
context: What do you want to achieve 1 year from now?
…3 years?
…5 years?

items.title: How important are these goals to you?
items.body: (If not important, remove them until you’re left with the most important goals.)
context: What do you want to achieve 1 year from now?
…3 years?
…5 years?
…10 years?

items.title: What are your action steps to achieve your first goal?
context: What do you want to achieve 1 year from now?
…3 years?
…5 years?
…10 years?
How important are these goals to you? (If not important, remove them until you’re left with the most important goals.)

items.title: What are your action steps to achieve your second goal?
context: What do you want to achieve 1 year from now?
…3 years?
…5 years?
…10 years?
How important are these goals to you? (If not important, remove them until you’re left with the most important goals.)
What are your action steps to achieve your first goal?

items.title: What are your action steps to achieve your other goals?
context: What do you want to achieve 1 year from now?
…3 years?
…5 years?
…10 years?
How important are these goals to you? (If not important, remove them until you’re left with the most important goals.)
What are your action steps to achieve your first goal?
What are your action steps to achieve your second goal?

items.title: Identify three people who have achieved your desired goals
What did they do to achieve the goals?
items.body: What can you learn from them?
context: Identify three people who have achieved your desired goals.

items.title: Are you putting any parts of your life on hold?
items.body: Why?

items.title: What is the top priority in your life right now?
items.body: What are you doing about it?

items.title: If you were to die tomorrow, what would be your biggest regret?
…What can you do now to make sure that it doesn’t happen?
context: If you were to die tomorrow, what would be your biggest regret?

items.title: Looking back on your life, have you done anything that you regretted?
…What happened, and why?
context: Looking back on your life, have you done anything that you regretted?

items.title: …What can you learn from this episode?
context: Looking back on your life, have you done anything that you regretted?
…What happened, and why?

items.title: …What can you do differently moving forward?
context: Looking back on your life, have you done anything that you regretted?
…What happened, and why?
…What can you learn from this episode?

items.title: Is there a grudge, a pain that you are holding on to?
…Why are you holding on to it?
context: Is there a grudge, a pain that you are holding on to?

items.title: …Is it time to let it go?
context: Is there a grudge, a pain that you are holding on to?
…Why are you holding on to it?

items.title: What is your biggest frustration right now?
…What can you do about it?
context: What is your biggest frustration right now?

items.title: What is the biggest thing you can do now to change your life for the better?
If you have a million dollars, what would you do with it?
Do you love your current job?
items.body: Why or why not?

items.title: What is your ideal career?
…What can you do to start working towards it?
context: What is your ideal career?

items.title: What is your ideal diet?
…Are you following your ideal diet now?
context: What is your ideal diet?

items.title: …If not, what can you do to move towards it?
context: What is your ideal diet?
…Are you following your ideal diet now?

items.title: What is your ideal home like?
…Is your current home a match with your ideal home?
context: What is your ideal home like?

items.title: …If not, what do you need to do to achieve your ideal home?
context: What is your ideal home like?
…Is your current home a match with your ideal home?

items.title: What is your ideal physical look?
…Is your current look a match with your ideal look?
context: What is your ideal physical look?

items.title: …If not, what do you need to do to achieve your ideal look?
context: What is your ideal physical look?
…Is your current look a match with your ideal look?

items.title: What is your ideal life?
…What do you need to do to start living your ideal life?
context: What is your ideal life?

items.title: What would you want to say to yourself in 10 years?
What do you fear most?
items.body: Why?

items.title: Is there anything you are running away from?
items.body: Why?

items.title: Are you settling for less than what you are worth?
items.body: Why?

items.title: What is your inner dialogue like?
items.body: Do you tend to think positive or negative thoughts?

items.title: Do you have limiting beliefs?
items.body: What are they?

items.title: Are they helping you to achieve your goals?
items.body: If not, is it time to let them go?
context: Do you have limiting beliefs? What are they?

items.title: What empowering beliefs can you replace them with?
context: Do you have limiting beliefs? What are they?
Are they helping you to achieve your goals? If not, is it time to let them go?

items.title: What bad habits do you want to break?
How can you break these bad habits?
context: What bad habits do you want to break?

items.title: What good habits do you want to cultivate?
How can you develop these good habits?
context: What good habits do you want to cultivate?

items.title: What is the meaning of life?
What is your life purpose?
items.body: What is your mission?

items.title: What drives you?
items.body: What are the times when you are most inspired, motivated, and charged up?

items.title: What did you do during those times?
items.body: How can you do more of that starting today?
context: What drives you? What are the times when you are most inspired, motivated, and charged up?

items.title: Who are your favorite people to hang out with?
Why?
items.body: How can you spend more time with them?
context: Who are your favorite people to hang out with?

items.title: You are the average of the 5 people you spend the most time with
items.body: Who are the 5 people you spend the most time with?

items.title: Are these people enabling you or holding you back?
context: You are the average of the 5 people you spend the most time with. Who are the 5 people you spend the most time with?

items.title: For the people holding you back, how can you spend less time with them?
context: You are the average of the 5 people you spend the most time with. Who are the 5 people you spend the most time with?
Are these people enabling you or holding you back?

items.title: Do you have any toxic relationships in your life?
items.body: If so, is it time to let them go?

items.title: Where can you meet people who can uplift you?
Is there someone whom you admire or respect?
What do you like about this person?
items.body: How can you be more like him/her?
context: Is there someone whom you admire or respect?

items.title: What qualities do you look for in your ideal partner?
Do you embody these qualities too?
context: What qualities do you look for in your ideal partner?

items.title: Are you afraid of letting others get close to you?
items.body: Why?

items.title: Who are the most important people to you in the world?
How can you spend more time with them starting today?
context: Who are the most important people to you in the world?

items.title: Describe the kind of person you enjoy spending time with
items.body: How can you be this person to others?

items.title: If you could choose anyone in the world, who would you like to be your mentor?
How can you learn from them (even if you don’t know them personally)?
context: If you could choose anyone in the world, who would you like to be your mentor?

items.title: How can you change someone’s life for the better today?
What are you going to do differently after reading this article?
items.note: In the source list, "this article" meant the list of 101 questions. Here, read it as the Daily Excellence essay the reader is reading right now: write about turning what you read into action, and invite the reader to name one thing they will do differently after reading today's essay.
